source.provenance: Drafted by an AI model for the course ladder in contemporary Bokmål (2005 norm); not reviewed by a native speaker. It is controlled, deliberately repetitive Norwegian written for learners and may contain unnatural phrasing. Facts about Norway and Bergen are general knowledge and unchecked. review.notes: Machine-drafted by an AI model; awaiting native-speaker review. House style: moderate Bokmål with three genders (ei/-a for feminine nouns, en/-en masculine, et/-et neuter), weak past in -et, neuter definite plural in -ene, sju and tjue, "ble", "ga". Prices are in kroner. The number words are written out so that the reader meets them.

sentences.text: Sam er på markedet. Han vil kjøpe mat.
sentences.english: Sam is at the market. He wants to buy food.

sentences.text: Marta er også på markedet. Hun selger brød.
sentences.english: Marta is also at the market. She sells bread.

sentences.text: God dag, Marta! Jeg vil kjøpe brød.
sentences.english: Hello, Marta! I want to buy bread.
sentences.speaker: sam

sentences.text: God dag, Sam! Hvor mye brød vil du ha?
sentences.english: Hello, Sam! How much bread do you want?
sentences.speaker: marta

sentences.text: Jeg tar to brød. Hvor mye koster det?
sentences.english: I will take two loaves. How much does it cost?
sentences.speaker: sam

sentences.text: Brødet koster tretti kroner.
sentences.english: The bread costs thirty kroner.
sentences.speaker: marta

sentences.text: Er det dyrt?
sentences.english: Is that expensive?
sentences.speaker: sam

sentences.text: Nei, det er ikke dyrt. Det er billig!
sentences.english: No, it is not expensive. It is cheap!
sentences.speaker: marta

sentences.text: Bra! Jeg tar tre brød.
sentences.english: Good! I will take three loaves.
sentences.speaker: sam

sentences.text: Tre brød koster nitti kroner.
sentences.english: Three loaves cost ninety kroner.
sentences.speaker: marta

sentences.text: Sam har penger. Han betaler nitti kroner.
sentences.english: Sam has money. He pays ninety kroner.

sentences.text: Takk, Sam! Ha det bra!
sentences.english: Thanks, Sam! Goodbye!
sentences.speaker: marta

sentences.text: Ola selger epler.
sentences.english: Ola sells apples.

sentences.text: Hei, Ola! Hva koster eplene?
sentences.english: Hi, Ola! What do the apples cost?
sentences.speaker: sam

sentences.text: To koster tjue kroner.
sentences.english: Two cost twenty kroner.
sentences.speaker: ola

sentences.text: Er det dyrt?
sentences.english: Is that expensive?
sentences.speaker: sam

sentences.text: Nei, nei! Det er billig!
sentences.english: No, no! It is cheap!
sentences.speaker: ola

sentences.text: Jeg tar fire epler.
sentences.english: I will take four apples.
sentences.speaker: sam

sentences.text: Det blir førti kroner.
sentences.english: That will be forty kroner.
sentences.speaker: ola

sentences.text: Jeg har penger. Jeg betaler nå.
sentences.english: I have money. I am paying now.
sentences.speaker: sam

sentences.text: Takk! Ha det bra, Sam!
sentences.english: Thanks! Goodbye, Sam!
sentences.speaker: ola

sentences.text: Sam har brød og mat. Han går hjem.
sentences.english: Sam has bread and food. He goes home.

sentences.text: Anna er hjemme. Hun er trøtt i dag.
sentences.english: Anna is at home. She is tired today.

sentences.text: Hei, Sam! Hva har du?
sentences.english: Hi, Sam! What do you have?
sentences.speaker: ana

sentences.text: Jeg har brød og mat.
sentences.english: I have bread and food.
sentences.speaker: sam

sentences.text: Er det dyrt?
sentences.english: Is that expensive?
sentences.speaker: ana

sentences.text: Nei, det er billig. Jeg betaler ikke mye.
sentences.english: No, it is cheap. I do not pay much.
sentences.speaker: sam

sentences.text: Nå har jeg ikke penger. Men jeg har mat!
sentences.english: Now I have no money. But I have food!
sentences.speaker: sam

sentences.text: Bra! Jeg liker brød. Vil du ha te, Sam?
sentences.english: Good! I like bread. Do you want tea, Sam?
sentences.speaker: ana

sentences.text: Ja, gjerne! Jeg er glad i dag.
sentences.english: Yes, please! I am happy today.
sentences.speaker: sam

sentences.text: Du kjøper mye, Sam. Du er glad!
sentences.english: You buy a lot, Sam. You are happy!
sentences.speaker: ana

sentences.text: Ja, jeg liker markedet. Det er bra.
sentences.english: Yes, I like the market. It is good.
sentences.speaker: sam

sentences.text: Fru Berg er også på markedet. Hun kommer fra kirka, og hun vil kjøpe brød.
sentences.english: Mrs Berg is also at the market. She comes from church, and she wants to buy bread.

sentences.text: Hvem er læreren din, Nils?
sentences.english: Who is your teacher, Nils?
sentences.speaker: marta

sentences.text: Det er Lars. Han er læreren min på skolen.
sentences.english: It is Lars. He is my teacher at the school.
sentences.speaker: nico

sentences.text: Marta lager middag. Hun lager fisk og poteter, og hun lager suppe.
sentences.english: Marta makes dinner. She makes fish and potatoes, and she makes soup.
